_readme: One setup per file, listed in CAMConfig.constants.setups in the order Machine Settings shows them. A custom setup is a copy of one of these with an id and a label of its own, added as a custom file (core/file-validation.json, kinds.setup).
logic names the code that writes the program: rs274 (BasePostProcessor), or makera, fanuc and winpcnc, which extend it and read the same flags. rml (Roland) declares its own.
flags: what the control accepts. Every key is required: no code fills in a missing one.

defaults: the value each Machine Settings field starts at while this setup is active, by field name; the operator may change it. locks: values the operator cannot change while it is active - a locked field shows 'Set by <label>' and is never stored.
The id is stored in settings: never rename one.
label: Grbl

_notes.supportsToolChange: TODO - Consider a manual tool change macro. Stops spindle, goes to origin, raises Z, allows change, probe? raise again, finally allows resume? Makera has a similar system?
_notes.rotary: Classic Grbl 1.1 is strictly XYZ - no A word, no G93. It still runs rotary work by axis replacement: wire the rotary to the Y driver and set $101 so 1 'mm' of Y is 1 mm of arc at the reference radius. That IS 'wrapped-linear': the developed strip needs no conversion whatsoever.
